subject: Invoice routing, min-commit phasing and tax responsibility (Order Form redlines)
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sable.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@sable.com>
Cc: Sable Legal <legal@sable.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify invoicing split & tax responsibility on Order Form redlines

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending the draft order form redlines this morning. A few quick clarifications from procurement and legal before we route:

1) Invoice routing: our accounting team needs invoices split by entity (Sable Systems, Sable UK Ltd). Can Redwood split the invoice by related account line items, or will Sable receive a single invoice and need to reallocate on our side? If Redwood can emit per-entity invoices, please confirm which billing entity will appear on each invoice for the minimum commit vs. usage surcharges.

2) Minimum commit phasing: procurement wants the initial minimum commit to be invoiced up-front for month 1 and prorated across the first quarter thereafter. Is there flexibility to move from a monthly trigger to a quarterly trigger for invoice issuance?

3) Tax responsibility and evidence: Sable will provide our VAT registration and a tax residency certificate (attached). Please confirm whether Redwood requires gross-up language in the order form or whether Sable will self-assess withholding when applicable.

We attached the tax certificate and flagged the places in the redline PDF where our legal had questions. If possible, can you loop in Redwood legal or the deal owner to confirm preferred flows?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our procurement deadline is EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Procurement | Sable Systems
Attachments: Sable_Tax_Certificate.pdf, Sable_Requested_Clarifications.pdf

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sable.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing split & tax responsibility on Order Form redlines

Emily —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick internal summary and next steps from our side:

- Invoice routing: Redwood can emit separate invoices per legal entity when the contract explicitly maps line-items to those entities. That requires the Order Form appendix to include an "invoice recipient" column for each SKU/band. I attached our updated redline (Sable_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf) where I inserted a billing-entity column for legal to sign off.

- Minimum commit phasing: Ben (cc'd, Finance) — can we support an initial up-front invoice for month 1 and then shift to quarterly issuance for the following two months (prorated), as Sable requests? If not fully supported, suggest a hybrid: up-front month 1 + monthly invoicing but with a credit true-up at quarter end.

- Tax responsibility: Kimberly (cc'd, Legal) — can you confirm whether we need gross-up language in the Order Form or if a certificate of tax residency + local VAT registration suffices to avoid withholding? Also please confirm any evidence we require from Sable for EU reverse charge handling.

Action items:
1) Kimberly to respond with legal's position on gross-up and required evidence.
2) Ben to confirm invoicing cadence options and implications for billing automation.
3) Grace to provide final redline PDF and DocuSign link once internal alignment complete.

I'll plan to follow up end of day tomorrow with the consolidated position so Sable can keep to their procurement deadline.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Sable_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf

If not fully supported, suggest a hybrid: up-front month 1 + monthly invoicing but with a credit true-up at quarter end.
>

Thanks Grace — below our legal position and required redline language.

1) Gross-up: we do not accept a unilateral gross-up for cross-border withholding. Standard practice: the payer is responsible for any applicable withholding tax unless a mutually agreed gross-up is included and specifically negotiated as part of commercial concessions. For this deal, we recommend Sable provide their tax residency certificate and Redwood will accept no withholding where local law and evidence permit reverse charge. If Sable requires Redwood to gross-up, this must be escalated to sales leadership and captured as a commercial concession (will affect price).

2) Evidence for reverse charge / VAT: we require (a) valid VAT registration number for the entity that will receive the supplies, and (b) a signed tax residency certificate if withholding relief is claimed. For UK/EU reverse charge we also accept the EU VAT checker output or equivalent confirmation. Attachments: Sable_Tax_Certificate.pdf (from procurement).

3) Invoice entity mapping: legal is fine with an invoice appendix that maps SKUs to billing entities, with the caveat that the master MSA must include a clause confirming Redwood's ability to issue multiple invoices for a single Order Form. I've proposed the following short clause to the MSA: "Redwood may issue invoices to multiple customer entities listed in the applicable Order Form; each invoice will only bind the invoiced entity for payment obligations reflected on that invoice." Please see Sable_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf where clause wording is tracked.

Next steps: Grace, please confirm whether Redwood can support the hybrid invoicing flow (up-front month 1 + monthly invoices + quarter true-up) or if Finance prefers quarterly issuance after month 1. If Sable insists on quarterly issuance only, Finance will advise on how to set up billing automation and any timing trade-offs.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sable.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing split & tax responsibility on Order Form redlines

Grace / Kimberly / Emily —

Quick finance update on feasibility and operational impact:

- We can support the hybrid approach: invoice month 1 up-front (charged as initial minimum commit), then issue monthly invoices for consumption and surcharges, and perform a quarter-end true-up credit/charge to reconcile the minimum commit phasing. This avoids building a new quarterly-only cadence in our billing system and keeps cashflow predictable.

- If Sable absolutely requires that the invoices are issued on a quarterly cadence (no monthly invoices), we can accommodate but require a small operational lead time: set up will take 7–10 business days to configure the account mapping and may delay first delivery of invoice PDFs to Sable's AR team.

- For per-entity invoices: we can emit separate invoices per legal entity as long as the Order Form explicitly maps SKUs to entities. There is a small per-invoice processing fee that we typically absorb for large deals, but if Sable requests more than 3 distinct invoice recipients we may need to include a nominal admin charge (we'll flag if applicable).

Next steps:
1) Grace to send the tracked redline with the invoice-entity column (done).
2) Emily to confirm Sable's preferred cadence: hybrid (recommended) or quarterly-only.
3) Once cadence confirmed, Redwood will provide final Order Form + DocuSign link.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
